To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
RAG reactivation in the CD4+CD88+ thymocyte stage is essential for secondary recombination and for generating TCR diversity.

(1) RAG reinducesion is essential for TCRα reassembly in vivo; (2) RAG reassembly occurs during the CD4+CD4+ stage of thymocyte development; (3) TCRα rearranges in a restricted region of the Jα gene segment cluster in mice lacking RAG reassembly; (4) TCRα reassembles in a secondary manner in the absence of RAGE reinduction; (5) the majority of
the second wave of TCRα reinduction in the thymus is required for secondary rearrangement and that secondary rearrangements are the major source of TCRα diversity in the periphery.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of lymphocytes in the thymus.
the molecular and cellular basis of thymocyte development and T cell receptor gene expression.
the molecular mechanisms that regulate T cell development in the thymus.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
RAG reexpression is essential to the generation of mature T cells.
RAG re-induction is not required for TCRα rearrangements in the first wave of T cells.
RAG re-induction is not required for TCRα re-combination but is required for secondary recombination and that a large proportion of mature TCRα genes are products of secondary rearrangement.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
RAG reactivation is essential for the generation of a normal thymocyte repertoire.
the RAG reinductin step is essential for the generation of a diverse TCRα chain repertoire in vivo, but that this step is not required for the initiation of TCRα rearrangements.
RAG reexpression is essential for the completion of the TCR repertoire in vivo, but is not required for the initial steps in TCRα gene rearrangement.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the second wave of TCRα recombining activity in CD4+8+ thymocyte is not essential for the initial rearrangement of the TCRa locus.
the second wave of recombination activating gene expression in thymocytes is required to generate a diverse T cell repertoire.
the majority of mature αβ T cells carry TCRα chains that are products of secondary rearrangement.
